commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[iris] Release capacity held by superseded preempted attempts (#11313)

Keep superseded worker-bound attempts in reconciliation until the worker
confirms termination. Preempted attempts previously disappeared from the
reconcile plan after a retry was assigned, while their unset finish
times kept worker capacity reserved and could block full-slice gangs.

Build each old attempt's stop or status-probe intent from its own state.
A terminal or MISSING observation finishes only that attempt and
releases its capacity; the newer attempt remains unchanged. Retries
assigned to the same worker wait for the old process to stop before
dispatch.

All five new regressions fail on main and pass with the fix.

This fix is not yet deployed. After deployment, existing superseded
PREEMPTED attempts with unset finish times re-enter reconciliation; a
terminal or MISSING worker response finishes each old attempt and
releases its capacity without changing the retry. No separate operator
mutation is needed for that state. [Worker logs for all 13 stranded
attempts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11289#issuecomment-6844342686)
record KILLED after cleanup while controller finish times remain unset;
these are historical observations, not fresh container inspections.

Fixes #11289

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[rl] Match Hero EP MuonH updates and checkpoint recipes (#11301)

Match the MuonH updates used by Hero's Levanter trainer. For each
layer's gate, up and down projections, Hero preserves the combined
Frobenius norm of all routed expert weights. The new
`optimizer_kwargs.expert_normalization: all_experts` option applies this
rule across GPUs. Each shared expert keeps separate norms for its
projections. Fused Q/K/V and gate/up weights are still updated as
separate matrices.

Per-expert normalization remains the default. Whole-bank mode rejects
routed expert names it cannot recognize. Both modes now round
coefficients and sums of squares to BF16, and transpose square matrices
before Newton–Schulz, matching the reference. Checkpoints record the
normalization mode and reject optimizer state saved with a different
mode.

CPU tests compare three updates with an independent JAX reference,
including experts split unevenly between processes. Both modes pass. The
largest relative L2 error in parameter changes is `9.46e-6`, below the
`1e-3` limit. The previous per-expert implementation fails both
reference comparisons.

A check on four GB200 GPUs saves a native Megatron checkpoint, restores
it with momentum in pinned CPU memory, and applies another update.
Weights, optimizer state and counters match an uninterrupted run bit for
bit. This check uses a small Hero model with supplied gradients; it does
not test forward/backward or serving.

Extracted from #11199 using main's dependency versions. The separate
AdamW restore repairs and Mochi launcher remain outside this change.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
Keep each SkyRL trainer and inference engine within one NVLink domain

On NVL72, keep the trainer within one rack and each vLLM inference engine within one rack when `iris.role_topology: nvlink.domain` is set. Each rack is one NVLink domain; different engines may occupy different racks. Iris admits the host groups as one job, and Ray pins each trainer or engine to its assigned group. The planner uses Iris’s schedulable-rack budget of 16 four-GPU hosts (64 GPUs); each trainer or engine must fit. Inference requires tensor and pipeline parallelism of one (TP=PP=1), with expert parallelism equal to data parallelism (EP=DP). Leaving the option unset preserves existing placement.

Use the same locality checks in Marin and the launcher. Marin rounds each group's GPU demand up to whole hosts. Policy-only DPO and checkpoint export can plan trainer placement without an inference role.

Carry the placement work from #11317 onto main after #11299. #11317 merged into `stack/cross-host-ep-11299`, leaving these changes off main. Two maintainers approved #11317 at 78974d46483a. The final Iris grouping changes and the planner fixes above followed those reviews. Use the admin override at the repository owner's request because GitHub does not transfer approvals to this follow-up PR. All required CI checks pass.

Deploy an Iris controller that includes this commit before enabling the mode. The mode drops the soft preference for nearby InfiniBand racks. Live admission and communication between trainer and inference racks still need validation.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Document per-task research logbook records (#11450)

Create a per-task index record after publishing the initial research
notebook. Update it when the research reaches a material result, changes
direction, ends, or its contribution links change.

Use a stable issue link in each Marin contribution PR so reviewers and
future automation can find the corresponding logbook. This follows the
per-task file migration in marin-community/marin-logbooks#44.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
Allow dev GPU sessions to pin their task image (#10773)

Dev GPU sessions now accept `--task-image`, so an experiment can keep
its container image fixed when the cluster default changes. Omitting it
keeps the existing default.

Validated by launching an eight-node, 32-GB200 session and checking that
every task pod used the requested image digest. Diff-scoped lint passed;
the affected-test selector found no affected test packages. Advisory
review found no issues.

Part of marin-community/marin-logbooks#19.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
Keep verified S3 copies stable across listing and HEAD metadata (#11432)

Keep using the listing's ETag after a copy when S3 HEAD also returns a
VersionId. Ignore `VersionId=null` when choosing a source identity; this
unversioned marker otherwise hides same-size overwrites in completed
copies.

`fsutil verified-copy` previously rejected an unchanged 13.8 MB fixture
in CoreWeave storage. The fixture now copies with its pinned SHA256, and
all 74 fsutil tests pass.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[rl] Allow cross-host expert-parallel resource planning (#11299)

Allow one vLLM inference engine to use GPUs on several machines when
training and inference use separate GPUs. For example, 48 training GPUs
and 12 inference GPUs need 15 machines with four GPUs each. Before this
change, both planners rejected this layout because the 12-GPU inference
engine cannot fit on one machine, even though the runtime already
supports it.

Update both Marin's launcher and SkyRL's resource planner to request
enough machines for this layout. Each inference worker uses one GPU, and
the model's experts are spread across all workers in that engine. Tensor
and pipeline parallelism must both be one (`TP=PP=1`). Expert
parallelism (`EP`) must equal data parallelism (`DP`), which is the
number of inference workers in this layout. Engines that fit on one
machine keep their existing placement rules.

CPU tests cover all nine combinations of 32, 48 or 64 training GPUs with
16, 32 or 64 inference GPUs, plus the demonstrated 48/12 layout and a
72-GPU trainer. Both planners produce matching machine counts. These
checks do not guarantee that an expert-parallel group stays within one
NVLink domain; it may communicate across the interconnect between hosts
or racks. GPU evidence comes from the earlier 48/12 Mochi run in #11199,
within one NVLink domain. Other layouts and the current dependency
versions still need GPU testing; no new GPU runs were performed here.

Extracted from #11199 at
[108c2888c7](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/108c2888c7aa66e771c802ba3a89ce374a1f331c).
#10948 chooses how inference workers are launched and changes the same
Marin planner, but keeps the one-machine limit. This fix does not depend
on it.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Let harnesses select context recovery (#11239)

Each harness declares one context-recovery policy for an attempt. The
shared model session applies it using its existing record of earlier
responses, while `start` and `reply` keep their previous signatures.
SkyRL's worker no longer duplicates that state or selects recovery by
harness name.

SkyRL's model adapter reports context refusals as `ContextRejected`,
retaining the original error. The session raises `ContextWindowExceeded`
when the harness permits recovery. Native agents can recover on first
and later requests; full Harbor trials can recover after a completed
model turn. Harbor's initial generation-budget rejection produces a
rollout with `stop_reason="length"`, and an initial serving failure
retains its original error. Grading, reward treatment, cleanup and
cumulative limits keep their existing behavior.

The same thirteen [public worker
checks](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d574c58573fca2cc2c67524379dc9c16e2556814/vendor/skyrl/cloud/iris/tests/test_agent_context_recovery.py)
pass on the clean base and refactored code. Follow up on #11235.
